title: MCP Server Settings
description: Configure the Model Context Protocol server. Exposes /mcp so AI agents can discover and query your site. Available on Pro and higher editions. Per-collection access is configured on each collection's schema (Phase 1).

enabled.label: Enable MCP Server
enabled.help: Master switch for the MCP endpoint. When off, /mcp returns 404 and discovery reports disabled: true. Defaults on for Pro+ editions.

publicAccess.label: Allow Public Access
publicAccess.help: Allow anonymous (no API key) callers to discover and use tools whose collection has mcp.access: 'public' set on its schema. Turn this off to require an API key for every MCP request, regardless of collection settings.

allowedOrigins.label: CORS Allowed Origins
allowedOrigins.placeholder: Pick a known AI client or type a custom origin
allowedOrigins.help:
Origins permitted to call /mcp from inside a browser tab. Pick a known browser-based AI client from the dropdown, or type a custom origin (e.g. https://example.com) for in-house playgrounds.

Native MCP clients (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Claude Code, MCP Inspector) connect regardless of this setting — CORS is a browser-only mechanism and never reaches non-browser clients. Server-side AI integrations are also unaffected.

Leave empty (default) to allow any origin — equivalent to * — so browser-based AI clients work out of the box. To restrict browser access, list specific origins instead. Note: an open policy lets any website's JavaScript read your public MCP surface from a visitor's browser (it can never reach auth-gated collections); if you have public-but-sensitive collections, list explicit origins.

publicIpPerMinute.label: Public Rate Limit (per minute)
publicIpPerMinute.help: Maximum MCP requests per minute from a single IP for unauthenticated (public persona) callers. Admin API key callers bypass this limit. Set to 0 to disable rate limiting for public callers.

toolPrefix.label: Tool Name Prefix
toolPrefix.help: Optional prefix prepended to every MCP tool name. Useful when running multiple T3 sites in the same AI agent so tools are distinguishable (e.g. bistro produces bistro_list_collections, bistro_query_collection). Leave blank for default names. Snake-case only, max 24 characters. Note: changing this requires connected AI clients (Claude Desktop, Inspector, etc.) to reconnect — existing sessions will see stale tool names until they re-initialize.

subscriptionsEnabled.label: Enable Resource Subscriptions
subscriptionsEnabled.help: When on, AI agents can call resources/subscribe on URIs like tcms://blog/ and T3 will push notifications/resources/updated when matching content changes. Clients on the 2026-07-28 specification use subscriptions/listen instead, which T3 filters by the caller's access — an agent is only ever told about resources it could read directly. When off, the SDK still accepts subscribe calls but T3 won't push notifications, and subscriptions/listen is refused outright rather than holding a worker to deliver nothing — the kill switch for production troubleshooting.

subscriptionStreamSeconds.label: Subscription Stream Duration (seconds)
subscriptionStreamSeconds.help: How long one subscriptions/listen stream stays open before closing on its own. That is the 2026-07-28 specification's replacement for resources/subscribe: a client opens one stream, names the resources it cares about, and receives updates until the window closes. Not the same as the Listening Stream Duration below — that one answers scanner probes with keepalives and nothing else, while this one carries real notifications, so there is an actual reason to hold it open. Each open stream holds one PHP worker for the whole window, and it shares the Max Concurrent Listening Streams ceiling below. Unlike the setting below, 0 is not a cheap option here — it means never close to the underlying SDK, so anything at or below zero is ignored and 1 second is used instead. To stop serving these streams at all, turn off Enable Resource Subscriptions.

listeningStream.label: Answer SSE Probes with a Listening Stream
listeningStream.help: Some MCP clients (e.g. OpenAI's plugin submission scanner) probe /mcp with a GET that asks for an SSE upgrade (Accept: text/event-stream) and treat the protocol-legal 405 response as a failure. When on, T3 answers those requests with a short keepalive-only SSE stream instead, auth- and Origin-checked identically to POST. A plain GET without the SSE Accept header always gets the normal 405, whatever this is set to. Each open stream holds one PHP-FPM worker for the duration below — turn this off under worker pressure and let the SDK return its normal 405.

listeningStreamSeconds.label: Listening Stream Duration (seconds)
listeningStreamSeconds.help: How long the listening stream (above) stays open before closing on its own. Clamped to 0-30 seconds no matter what's entered here. 0 is the cheapest setting that still passes a probe — the client still gets a real 200 text/event-stream response with a keepalive event in it, but the worker is released in milliseconds instead of held for the whole window. Behind a buffering reverse proxy (Cloudflare, nginx with proxy_buffering on) the worker is held for the full duration even after the real client disconnects, so keep this as short as your scanning clients accept.

listeningStreamMaxConcurrent.label: Max Concurrent Listening Streams
listeningStreamMaxConcurrent.help: Hard ceiling on streams opened site-wide per window, across all callers, covering both the listening stream above and subscriptions/listen. Both hold a PHP worker from the same pool, so they share one budget — separate caps would let the pair reach twice this number. This is the only limit that applies to OAuth-authenticated clients — the public rate limit above exempts anyone sending an Authorization: Bearer header — and the only one that bounds the total rather than a single IP. Keep it a small fraction of your pm.max_children: every worker a stream holds is taken from real request handling. Over the cap, probes get the normal 405 and subscription streams get a 503 telling them to retry. Set to 0 to disable the cap.

listeningStreamRetryMs.label: Listening Stream Reconnect Delay (ms)
listeningStreamRetryMs.help: How long a client is told to wait before reconnecting after the stream closes, sent as the SSE retry: field. A client occupies a worker for the duration above, then idles for this long, so raising it lowers the steady-state cost of every connected client proportionally. Nothing is lost while disconnected: T3 never pushes unsolicited messages over this stream — subscription notifications are delivered on the client's next request. Some clients ignore this and reconnect immediately; those are bounded by the cap above.
